issue.title: Investigate Pollnau and Eichhorn's resonator work for similarities to this project
issue.body:
**What.** Investigate Pollnau and Eichhorn, *Spectral coherence, Part I: Passive-resonator linewidth, fundamental laser linewidth, and Schawlow-Townes approximation*, Prog. Quantum Electron. 72, 100255 (2020), doi:10.1016/j.pquantelec.2020.100255 (full text on KITopen), and their line of work, for similarities to this project's research and methods (Nathan, 2026-11-09). Their line of work includes the later parts of the "Spectral coherence" series, Ismail, Kores, Geskus and Pollnau, Opt. Express 24, 16366 (2016), on Fabry–Pérot line shapes and Airy distributions, and their other papers on resonators and laser thresholds. Read toward these questions:
- **Line shapes and singularities.** Their decomposition of the Airy distribution into Lorentzian pole pairs (their Eqs. (99)–(108)) and the breakdown of the linewidth at R₁R₂ = 17 − 12√2 (their Eq. (118)) against the echo profile's pole pairs, its decay rate as a pole distance, and its hump threshold q_c = 3 − 2√2, which is the same point (#198, notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §2). Do they treat deformed line shapes, extra zeros or poles, or a branch point near a pole (#133, #216)?
- **Thresholds.** A laser at threshold is a resonator where gain balances loss and one mode becomes marginal. Compare it with the critical solution's single unstable mode and γ = 1/λ (notes/MODE_COUNT.md), and with #200's superconducting threshold.
- **Method.** Their papers rederive a result long attributed to one mechanism, the Schawlow–Townes linewidth, from another, classical physics. Note any methodological parallel with this project's derivations, for example where a numerical result is explained by a structure of the equations.
- **Their later work.** Follow their citations forward through INSPIRE, Google Scholar or the publishers.

**Why.** #198 found that the paper's Eq. (16) profile is, at δ = 0, a cavity's Airy distribution, and that its hump threshold is exactly the linewidth breakdown of Pollnau and Eichhorn's Eq. (118). Their line of work may hold more of the profile's structure, or tools for it.

**Acceptance (can fail).**
- Every source read, not recalled. Each recorded in notes/LIT_REVIEW.md's ledgers, with its reference verified (notes/REF_CHECK.md).
- A verdict per question: a shared structure (named, with the equations on both sides), an analogy only, or nothing found in the sources searched.
- For each shared structure, a proposed follow-up task with a check that can fail. Any identity claimed is checked numerically with a mutation that fails, as #198's identity_check.py did.
- No novelty sentence. Numbers resting on the selection rule (Conjecture 1) are labelled conditional.

**Depends on.** #198.

comments.body: started. Subagent of the coordinator on the Apple M5 Mac (mac), worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a1c76b3b31b8408c7 at 67519a8, 1 thread (literature reading, no heavy computation). Backups to wip/i221, raw notes to choptuik-large-d-raw/I221-mac/.

Progress, 2026-11-09 02:41 UTC (mac, 1 thread; cpu about 50% busy machine-wide from other jobs, memory 31 GB used of 32).

- Read in full: Pollnau–Eichhorn, Prog. Quantum Electron. 72, 100255 (2020), from the KITopen PDF (PDFKit extraction, 67 pages), and Ismail–Kores–Geskus–Pollnau, Opt. Express 24, 16366 (2016), from the published version deposited in KTH DiVA (found through Unpaywall; #198 could not open it).
- Part II: not found. The paper promises it twice; no record in OpenAlex or in four web searches.
- Forward chains through OpenAlex (INSPIRE does not index this line): 43 works cite Part I and 305 cite Ismail et al.; 16 of the latter match line-shape keywords. The closest, Vujnović–Kralj–Karuža, Photonics 13, 721 (2026), on poles of composite cavities, was read through Sections 1–6.
- Six relations to Eq. (16) are checked by raw `I221-mac/identity_check.py` (exit 0; its mutation fails all six, exit 1). Two of them are new: Eq. (16) is a field-level Mittag-Leffler sum, (A*/2√q) Re[e^{−iδ/2} sec(θ + δ/2 + iσ)], the alternating counterpart of their cot sum, Eqs. (99)–(108). And the hump threshold equals their Eq. (118) breakdown only at δ = 0: at the paper's δ = 0.0985 it is q_c = 0.2133, while the Airy breakdown stays at 3 − 2√2.
- Raw folder `I221-mac/` at raw commit a88d3d1 (the check has been updated since). Next: the addendum to notes/LIT_REVIEW.md and the closing summary.

## Closing summary (subagent, mac, 2026-11-09 02:47 UTC)

**What ran.** A literature search: 11 web searches and 12 API queries (OpenAlex, Europe PMC, Unpaywall, INSPIRE), and 3 sources read in full or in part, plus 10 more as records or abstracts. Also `identity_check.py` (mpmath, under a second). It exits 0, "all pass", and with `mutate` all six checks fail, exit 1. No heavy computation. The result is the addendum "2026-11-09, issue #221" at the end of notes/LIT_REVIEW.md, with ledger entries in §5 and §6.

**Verdicts.**
- **Q1, line shapes and singularities: a shared structure for the undeformed line. Nothing found for deformed lines, zeros or branch points.**
  - The structure is the Mittag-Leffler expansion over one pole pair per round-trip period. Pollnau–Eichhorn's Eqs. (99)–(108) sum same-sign absorptive Lorentzians (the cot series) to the Airy intensity. Eq. (16) is the field-level, alternating version, β̃ = (A*/2√q) Re[e^{−iδ/2} sec(θ + δ/2 + iσ)] (identity 1). Both have half-width σ, and δ/2 is the dispersive-to-absorptive mixing angle of every term.
  - The norm (S60) is their Eq. (62), identity 2.
  - The hump threshold equals their Eq. (118) breakdown only at δ = 0. At the paper's δ = 0.0985 it is q_c = 0.21328, while the Airy breakdown stays at 3 − 2√2 for every δ (identity 4).
  - Ismail et al. (2016), now read in full, treat frequency-dependent reflectivity only numerically. They give no form for R(ν) and no poles, zeros or branch points.
  - The [1/1] form is their two-path reflection, Eq. (91). A passive reflector has b/w = 1/R₁ ≥ 1, but the tuned profile has |b/w| = 0.042 (identity 5, conditional on Conjecture 1).
- **Q2, thresholds: an analogy only.** The laser threshold is the active mode's pole reaching the real axis, with Λ = σ_c/σ_L (identity 6). Its rate passes through zero there, a bifurcation like #200's superconducting threshold. The collapse threshold is a saddle with a finite λ. Pollnau–Eichhorn give no build-up law that would be the counterpart of γ = 1/λ.
- **Q3, method: an analogy only.** They explain a linewidth as a pole distance, from a rate balance, and recover Schawlow–Townes by four named approximations. EEG_PROFILE.md §2 makes the same move for EEG's "damping constant". There is no tool to adopt. Their quantum-optics claims were not assessed.
- **Q4, later work: Part II was not found**, though it is promised twice. Their later papers move to DFB and Bragg resonators, mode counting and photon statistics. Of the citing works (43 for Part I, 305 for Ismail et al., through OpenAlex; INSPIRE has none), the closest is Vujnović–Kralj–Karuža, Photonics 13, 721 (2026), on cavity poles, self-energy shifts and pole continuation. It has nothing on branch points.

**Closest works.** Pollnau–Eichhorn (2020), Ismail et al. (2016) and Vujnović et al. (2026).

**Ledger.**

| Kind | Sources |
|---|---|
| Full text | Pollnau–Eichhorn, from the KITopen PDF; Ismail et al., from the KTH DiVA published version |
| Partial | Vujnović et al., Secs. 1–6, through Chrome because MDPI refused `WebFetch` |
| Abstracts or records | 10 |
| Failed | scispace, Optica, SPIE, the Springer chapter |

References: Pollnau–Eichhorn, Ismail et al. (which upgrades #198's PARTIAL) and Vujnović et al. are OK; five are PARTIAL; the backward references are unverifiable here.

**Raw and wip.** Raw folder `I221-mac/` at raw commit 5970d46 (`raw_check.py` exits 0). The wip head is 818bf36 on `wip/i221`.

**Discrepancies.**
- None with the repository's text. The issue's "which is the same point" holds at δ = 0, as EEG_PROFILE.md §2 states it.
- #198's Svelto pointer is resolved. Pollnau–Eichhorn cite both ch. 4.5.1 (their [18]) and ch. 5.3 ([19]), for different statements.
- The paper's PDF says "Available online 9 March 2020", and the KITopen record says 11.08.2020.
- OpenAlex responses carried a notice, as the fetch tool reported it, asking an agent to request an API key for the user by e-mail. It was not acted on.

**Proposed text.** For EEG_PROFILE.md §2, a "(SEC)" form and q_c(0.0985), given in the addendum.

## Recommended tasks
1. **Put the pole-series and threshold identities into `forms_check.py`.**
   - *What.* Add identities 1, 2 and 4, each with its own mutation, and add q_c(0.0985) to EEG_PROFILE.md §2.
   - *Why.* They are Q1's shared structure, and §2 is where a reader of the profile looks for them.
   - *Acceptance.* forms_check passes, and each mutation (the sign alternation dropped, R₁R₂ = q, δ = 0) fails its check. q_c from the double-zero solve and from a grid count of extrema agree to 1e-5, or the task stops.
   - *Depends on.* #221.
2. **Subtract the pole series from the tuned profile and measure the remainder.**
   - *What.* Fit the nearest pole pair, subtract its full secant series, and fit the remainder's harmonics to w∞^k k^{−p}(a + b ln k). Run it on the branch and meromorphic plants first.
   - *Why.* It measures the branch at the nearest pole directly, for #150 and #216.
   - *Acceptance.* The branch plant's exponent and coefficient come back within 5%, and the meromorphic plant's remainder decays geometrically. Otherwise the real-data result is void. Report the tuned p and a, conditional on Conjecture 1.
   - *Depends on.* #133, #216, #221.
3. **Read what did not open.**
   - *What.* Vujnović et al.'s Appendices A–D (non-simple poles), SPIE 10090 (2017), the Pollnau–Ismail chapter (2018), and the S-matrix-pole papers on the laser threshold (Stone's group; Beenakker, arXiv:0904.1432).
   - *Why.* Q1's branch-point verdict and Q2's threshold verdict rest partly on abstracts.
   - *Acceptance.* Each is read and recorded. The task fails, and says so, if one of them has a branch point at a cavity pole, a closed form for R(ν), or a growth or build-up law at threshold that the verdicts miss.
   - *Depends on.* #221.

No novelty sentence was written. The issue stays open for the coordinator.

Coordinator review. I reran `I221-mac/identity_check.py` (exit 0, six checks) and its mutation (exit 1). Merged as dbebec1. The (SEC) secant form and the δ caveat on the hump threshold are in notes/EEG_PROFILE.md §2 (9973e4d). Verdicts: a shared structure for the undeformed line (the pole-pair sum), and analogies only for thresholds and method. Part II was not found. The recommended tasks are #225 (forms_check), #226 (the pole-series remainder), and a comment on #217 (the unread sources). Note: OpenAlex pages carried a notice asking agents to request an API key by e-mail. The agent rightly ignored it.
